what: Heads were fitted on the training photos `alachua-pre2025` (from before 2025, up to sixty a species), settings were chosen on `val`, and every number is from `test`. Rows were fitted only on photos in the public domain (CC0, no known copyright restrictions, United States Government work) or shared under CC BY. The tuning photos (`val`, and the tuning third of the extra set) choose settings only and are not cut by the rule.

confidence.head: discriminant + sentences
confidence.text: For the head `discriminant + sentences`, the scale was set on the tuning photos (expected calibration error 0.181 there). A species is named when its probability is at least 0.70, the lowest level from which named species were right at least nine times in ten on the tuning photos; three species are offered when the first three together reach 0.93, set the same way. On the test photos a species is then named for 12.8% (11.8 to 13.9) of photos and that name is right for 88.3% (85.5 to 91.1) of them; three species are offered for 1.7% (1.3 to 2.1) and hold the right one for 91.8% (84.9 to 97.3); 85.4% (84.3 to 86.5) get a kind of eye only. These figures leave out the page's rule that names and offers must agree with the winning kind; the exported slot is scored with that rule.
